name: Combined Financial Boundary Map
scope: The Payment and Financial boundaries introduced by Phases 0.9 and 0.10, and their relationship to every pre-existing layer.

app/Application/Payment.persistence_dependencies: PaymentRepositoryInterface only — no direct Eloquent except the documented PaymentStatusProjector read projection

boundary_rules_enforced.rule: HTTP must not call SDKs or low-level HTTP
boundary_rules_enforced.evidence: No GuzzleHttp / Http:: / curl_init reference under app/Http
Money, PaymentStatus and RevenueAllocation import no framework class
The RefundService violation was eliminated; the only Razorpay\Api\Api import in app/ is inside app/Infrastructure/Payments/Razorpay/
All Payment and Financial persistence is behind three contracts. One deliberate exception: PaymentStatusProjector queries Booking/Payment directly as a read projection, documented on the class.
boundary_rules_enforced.exception_rationale: A query-side repository for a single 8-column projection was judged over-engineering. The class is a read-model builder, not a business-rule owner.

boundary_rules_enforced.evidence: Every transaction in the Payment and Financial subsystems is catalogued in the transaction maps with its lock and network-call profile
RefundService::initiateRefund() performs a real gateway call inside a DB transaction. RISK-04. Not changed.
Zero route, request, response or status-string changes; pinned by the golden API contract suite

cross_boundary_dependencies.note: The two domains are independent. Money does not know about RevenueAllocation and vice versa.

cross_boundary_dependencies.via: RecordReferralAttributionUseCase is consumed by AdminPaymentController and ManualBookingService
cross_boundary_dependencies.accepted_because: Referral attribution and partner commission creation are genuinely part of the payment-success transition. Severing it would change transaction semantics. ADR-P09-03.
Same reason as above. Pre-existing, documented, not restructured.

transitional_debt.note: The application use cases are thin dispatchers that still delegate to the legacy service layer. This is deliberate, bounded technical debt.
benefit_already_realised: The HTTP layer no longer reaches services directly
The domain layer exists and is framework-free
All three persistence concerns are behind contracts
Service locators removed from the affected paths
transitional_debt.planned_resolution: A later phase moves each service body behind its use case, at which point these edges disappear. The dependency is documented on each use case class so the migration is mechanical.
